statement: A release changelog must distinguish scoring projections from whole-report byte equality and name the exact tree measured. The final 0.4.9 rubric record said all 24 reports differed after adding an optional behaviour fingerprint, while the CLI changelog and reproduction guide still said 20 were identical from an earlier candidate. Compare both records after the last format change, and explain documentation-only differences between the measured commit and immutable tag instead of claiming they are the same commit.

A package version executing correctly does not prove source provenance. During 0.4.9 finish-line checks, npm served 0.4.9 but omitted gitHead and dist.attestations and returned HTTP 404 from its attestation endpoint; the independently published OCI image did have source provenance. Report the channel-specific gap, keep the independent verifier red, and repair publishing in the next immutable version. Never copy a different channel or older version proof forward to make the release look complete.

A download-and-checksum recipe must stop execution when either download or verification fails. A site recipe that prints a checksum result and then independently runs chmod and the binary can execute a leftover or corrupt file after verification fails. Prefix the recipe with fail-fast shell behavior and test a deliberately wrong checksum to prove the executable is never invoked; also run the real release URL recipe and report a missing asset as a failure rather than a completed verification.
